sact_blessing.name: Blessing
sact_blessing.definition: A performative speech that bestows divine favor, prosperity, protection, or identity.
notes: They confer identity, destiny, and favor.
sact_blessing.searle_gloss: makes something so by saying it

cites.claim: David blesses the LORD and people

messages.name: Blessed are those who wash their robes

sact_cursing.name: Cursing
sact_cursing.definition: A performative speech that declares judgment, misfortune, or divine opposition.
sact_cursing.searle_gloss: makes something so by saying it

sact_oath.name: Oath
sact_oath.definition: A solemn, binding declaration invoking God as witness.
notes: They often seal covenants or agreements.

refrain.title: As surely as the LORD lives
As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD

sact_vow.name: Vow
sact_vow.definition: A voluntary promise made to God, often conditional.
notes: They express devotion, dependence, or desperation.
Breaking vows is serious covenant breach.

sact_naming.name: Naming
sact_naming.definition: A speech‑act that confers identity, destiny, or meaning by assigning a name.
sact_naming.searle_gloss: makes something so by saying it

cites.claim: God renames Abram → Abraham; Sarai → Sarah
John the Baptist named by God
Rachel names Ben‑oni; Jacob renames Benjamin

messages.name: You are the light of the world
You are the salt of the earth

events.name: Man and Woman in the Garden

refrain.title: She gave birth to a son

sact_commissioning.name: Commissioning
sact_commissioning.definition: A speech‑act assigning mission, authority, or responsibility.
sact_commissioning.searle_gloss: makes something so by saying it

instances.overlay: "Moses My servant is dead. Now therefore arise, you and all these people, and cross over the Jordan into the land I am giving them": God's charge to Joshua; nothing in the verse marks it as a commission but the story (Deut 31:23, already counted, is its announcement).

cites.claim: Adam commissioned to rule and cultivate
Abraham commissioned to go and become a blessing
Jacob commissioned to return to the land
Moses commissioned at the burning bush

sact_benediction.name: Benediction
sact_benediction.definition: A blessing spoken at the end of a discourse or gathering.
sact_benediction.searle_gloss: makes something so by saying it

cites.claim: “The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.”

events.name: David made king over Judah & all Israel

sact_petition.name: Petition
sact_petition.definition: A request for help, intervention, or provision.
sact_petition.searle_gloss: tries to get the hearer to act

cites.claim: Moses petitions for Israel after the golden calf

sact_intercession.name: Intercession
sact_intercession.definition: A speech‑act pleading on behalf of others.
sact_intercession.searle_gloss: tries to get the hearer to act

events.name: Abraham negotiates for Sarah’s burial cave

sact_lament.name: Lament
sact_lament.definition: A speech‑act expressing grief, complaint, sorrow, or protest before God.
notes: Lament is faithful protest, not unbelief.
It is the speech of suffering covenant loyalty.
It often leads to renewed trust.
sact_lament.searle_gloss: voices the speaker's state toward something

events.name: David made king over Judah & all Israel
Josiah’s reforms & book of the law
Abraham negotiates for Sarah’s burial cave

sact_complaint.name: Complaint
sact_complaint.definition: A speech‑act expressing dissatisfaction, grievance, or protest.
notes: Complaint = honest protest within covenant relationship.

cites.claim: “O LORD, how many are my foes.”
“Help us, O God of our salvation.”
“How long shall I cry for help?”

sact_thanksgiving.name: Thanksgiving
sact_thanksgiving.definition: A speech‑act expressing gratitude for God’s actions.
notes: It is the speech of memory + gratitude.
sact_thanksgiving.searle_gloss: voices the speaker's state toward something

sact_praise.name: Praise
sact_praise.definition: A speech‑act declaring God’s greatness, attributes, or deeds.
notes: It centers on God’s character and actions.
It is the speech of joy, awe, and worship.
sact_praise.searle_gloss: voices the speaker's state toward something

sact_doxology.name: Doxology
sact_doxology.definition: A formal expression of praise to God.
sact_doxology.searle_gloss: voices the speaker's state toward something

cites.claim: praise from the ends of the earth

refrain.title: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel

sact_confession_of_sin.name: Confession of sin
sact_confession_of_sin.definition: A speech‑act acknowledging guilt, wrongdoing, or covenant breach.

cites.claim: high priest confesses sins of Israel

sact_testimony.name: Testimony
sact_testimony.definition: A speech‑act declaring truth, witness, or personal experience.

cites.claim: “I will tell what He has done.”

themes.name: Father, Son And Holy Spirit (The Trinity)

sact_confession_of_faith.name: Confession of faith
sact_confession_of_faith.definition: A speech‑act declaring belief, allegiance, or trust.

instances.overlay: "you are to declare before the LORD your God, 'My father was a wandering Aramean'": Israel's set creed; the formula that introduces it ("say before the LORD") was tried as a rule and found 3 confessions in 23.

cites.claim: “The LORD is my light and my salvation.”
Martha: “I believe you are the Christ”

themes.name: Father, Son And Holy Spirit (The Trinity)

sact_promise.name: Promise
sact_promise.definition: A speech‑act declaring future blessing or action.

messages.name: I will give you a new heart
I will pour out my Spirit
Behold, I make all things new
The Lamb will be your light
The nations will walk in its light

sact_warning.name: Warning
sact_warning.definition: A speech‑act alerting to danger, judgment, or consequences.
sact_warning.searle_gloss: tries to get the hearer to act

cites.claim: Zephaniah warns of the Day of the Lord

messages.name: Sin is crouching at the door
Your sin will find you out
The day of the Lord is near
The axe is at the root
The judge is standing at the door
Every secret thing will be revealed

sact_summons.name: Summons
sact_summons.definition: A speech‑act calling someone into presence, action, or judgment.
sact_summons.searle_gloss: tries to get the hearer to act

cites.claim: Heaven and earth summoned as witnesses

messages.name: Hear the word of the Lord
Prepare the way of the Lord
The kingdom of God is at hand
Come out of her, my people

sact_command.name: Command
sact_command.searle_gloss: tries to get the hearer to act

messages.name: Do not repay evil for evil
Do not be wise in your own eyes
Walk in the way of wisdom
Avoid the path of the wicked

refrain.title: Just as the LORD had commanded
Commandments I am giving you today
This is what the LORD has commanded

sact_rebuke.name: Rebuke
sact_rebuke.searle_gloss: voices the speaker's state toward something

cites.claim: Proverbs: “Better open rebuke than hidden love”

sact_accusation.name: Accusation
sact_accusation.definition: A speech‑act charging someone with wrongdoing.

sact_defence.name: Defence
sact_defence.definition: A speech‑act responding to accusation with justification or explanation.

sact_taunt.name: Taunt
sact_taunt.definition: A speech‑act mocking an enemy or idol.
notes: Taunt = judgment + reversal + humiliation of evil.
sact_taunt.searle_gloss: voices the speaker's state toward something

sact_boast.name: Boast
sact_boast.definition: A speech‑act declaring confidence or pride — either righteous or sinful.

cites.claim: “My soul makes its boast in the LORD.”
“Let him who boasts boast in this…”
“Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”
“My soul makes its boast in the LORD.”
“We boast in God all day long.”
“Let him who boasts boast in this…”

sact_refusal.name: Refusal
sact_refusal.definition: A speech‑act declining a request, command, or offer.

cites.claim: Pharaoh: “I will not let Israel go.”
Israel refuses to enter the land
Rich young ruler refuses Jesus’ call
Bridegroom refuses entry to foolish virgins

sact_riddle.name: Riddle
sact_riddle.definition: A speech‑act using mystery or metaphor to conceal and reveal truth.
sact_riddle.searle_gloss: tries to get the hearer to act

events.name: The Complaint of Miriam and Aaron

sact_call_and_response.name: Call and response
sact_call_and_response.definition: A dialogical speech‑act where God calls and the people respond.
notes: Call/response = covenant ratification + worship + communal identity.
sact_call_and_response.searle_gloss: more than one kind in one form

cites.claim: Covenant ceremony (“All the LORD has spoken we will do”)
Spirit and Bride say “Come” → hearer responds

messages.name: The Spirit and the Bride say, ‘Come’

sact_lament_over_a_city.name: Lament over a city
sact_lament_over_a_city.definition: A speech‑act grieving over a city’s sin or impending destruction.
sact_lament_over_a_city.searle_gloss: voices the speaker's state toward something

sact_last_words.name: Last words
sact_last_words.definition: Final speech‑acts spoken before death or departure.
notes: Last words = legacy + blessing + warning + identity.
sact_last_words.searle_gloss: more than one kind in one form

performative.name: Performative speech
performative.desc: Speech that does what it says: it blesses, curses, binds, names or sends.

prayer.name: Prayer
prayer.desc: Speech addressed to God: asking, pleading for others, grieving, protesting, thanking, praising, confessing.

proclamation.name: Proclamation
proclamation.desc: Speech that declares or directs: bearing witness, confessing faith, promising, warning, summoning, commanding.

confrontation.name: Confrontation
confrontation.desc: Speech that meets another head on: rebuking, accusing, defending, taunting, boasting, refusing.

forms.name: Set forms of speech
forms.desc: Recognised shapes of speaking: the riddle, the call and its answer, the lament over a city, last words.
